summary: npm package ships only an obfuscated HTML redirector page
details: The tarball contains a single file, index.html, declared as the package `main`. The HTML renders a Cloudflare Turnstile-themed 'verification' page containing obfuscator.io-style JavaScript that, on Turnstile callback, reconstructs a target URL and calls window.location.replace to redirect the browser. package.json declares no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare lifecycle scripts, and npm cannot require an HTML `main`, so installing or importing this package performs no code execution on a developer machine. The obfuscated redirect only fires if a human opens index.html in a browser and completes the Turnstile widget; the target audience is browser visitors, not npm installers. The package appears to be abuse of the npm registry as static hosting for an obfuscated redirector / likely phishing landing page rather than a supply-chain attack against installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
